name: 从灰里走出来的人
src: 诸国期/诸国期时段_一_晨祷.md:1709
who: The man who walked out of the ash, a human of no certain age who came out of the burnt town of Pinegate in early spring and cannot say who he is: he could be twenty-five or forty, about 176 cm, lean and spare. His hair is so thick with grey ash that its own colour cannot be told, ash in the lashes and the brows. Pale clear green eyes, blank and searching. Black earth is packed under every fingernail and into the creases of both hands. His head keeps turning a little to one side, as if looking down a street that is no longer there. No jewellery, no glasses. A quiet, lost, unhurried air; he does not speak.
face: FACE, as in the references: a lean man's face of no clear age, hollow at the cheeks, pale clear green eyes wide and blank, brows and lashes greyed with ash, a straight nose, a closed mouth that seems about to open and does not, a faint smear of ash and earth along one cheekbone. Clean pale skin under the dust; skin shadows a soft cool tone.
build: 176 cm, lean and spare: narrow shoulders, long arms, a light walk.
palette: ash grey, burnt umber, black earth, pale spring green, faded oatmeal
casual: As he came out of the ash: a coarse long-sleeved tunic and trousers whose first colour is lost under grey ash and black earth, the cuffs and hem scorched ragged, an old wool cloak burnt short at the hem hanging from one shoulder, the feet wrapped in strips of sacking. His hands hang open at his sides, black earth under every nail and in the creases of the palms. The head turned a little to one side, a blank searching look.
private: His winter in the village at the edge of the burnt land: a borrowed undyed wool shirt too wide for him, buttoned down the front, plain brown trousers, a coarse grey blanket wrapped round the shoulders, borrowed felt boots. He holds a wooden bowl of food in both hands, the earth still in his nail beds, the ash still dulling his hair. A quiet, faraway look.
battle: Walking out of the ash: the same scorched, ash-caked tunic and trousers, the burnt wool cloak hanging from one shoulder, the feet wrapped in sacking. He carries nothing and has never fought; both hands hang open and loose, black earth packed under the nails, the head turned a little to one side, the green eyes blank.
battle_pose: 3) the walking-out outfit: standing still and upright, both empty hands open and loose at his sides with the earth-blackened fingers spread, the head turned a little to one side as if looking for a street, no weapon, a blank searching look.
formal: Washed for the village's midwinter fire: a borrowed clean grey-brown wool tunic buttoned down the front with fitted sleeves, a plain belt, an old sheep-wool cloak pinned at the shoulder, the hair still faintly grey with ash that will not wash out, earth still in the nail beds. He holds a small lit clay lamp in both hands and looks down into its flame. A still, quiet look.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face large, turned a little aside, the pale green eyes caught by a small lamp flame off to one side and not looking at the viewer. Cold grey early-spring light from the front, a small warm lamp glow on one cheek. Foreground blur: drifting flakes of grey ash and a few fresh blades of grass.
gear: 启源（估）｜贫｜不打仗｜1档｜身份不裁定，从烧光的城里走出来，什么也不拿、不出手，第三格照姿势句空手站着，衣裳还是那一身焦灰。
